title: Same House. Theo Pays $107K More 😬
description:
Same house. Same $300,000 mortgage. Nora's credit score is 760 and she gets 6%. Theo's is 620 and he gets 7.5%. "It's only one and a half percent," says Theo. That's $299 more every month (about $1,799 vs $2,098), and over 30 years Theo pays $107,637 more interest for the exact same house.

Takeaway: on a big loan, your credit score is one of the biggest numbers you'll ever pay for. Paying on time and keeping card balances low are what move it.

Would you fix your score first, or buy now and refinance later? 👇

Follow for more numbers that change how you spend.

⚠️ Assumptions: example rates for illustration only (real rates depend on the lender, market and your full application); $300,000 30-year fixed loan, monthly payments, principal and interest only (no property taxes, insurance, PMI or fees). Fictional characters. This is not financial advice.
